report.source_text: Therapy according to the Euro-Lupus protocol was initiated, consisting of an intravenous steroid pulse (500 mg/day for 3 days), followed by oral methylprednisolone 0.8 mg/kg/day during the first month, afterwards slowly tapering the dose to 0.1 to 0.2 mg/kg/day. Cyclophosphamide (500 mg/day) was given six times, with an interval of 2 weeks. Along with this therapy, protective measures for gastrointestinal disease, candida infections, Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, herpes infection, and osteoporosis was started. With this treatment regimen, disease control was obtained with complete clearance of the skin eruption and a normal urinalysis without proteinuria nor hematuria within 3 months after the start of treatment. DNA Farr titer became negative, and there was no more complement consumption. Steroids were tapered, and azathioprine as maintenance therapy was initiated at a dose of 1 mg/kg/day with maintained disease control during 4 months of follow-up.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old woman presented with a photosensitive erythematous maculopapular rash on sun-exposed skin areas. Initial evaluation revealed positive antinuclear factor including U1RNP, high anti-dsDNA Farr titer, hypocomplementemia, proteinuria (0.33 g/24h), massive hematuria, increased urinary white blood cells, and normal kidney size on ultrasound with CKD G2 stage. Due to pathological proteinuria and serologic abnormalities, a kidney biopsy was performed. Histopathology revealed focal crescentic and focal mesangial glomerular damage with full immunohistochemical positivity for IgA, IgG, and C1q, consistent with lupus nephritis. The patient was treated according to the Euro-Lupus protocol with steroids and cyclophosphamide followed by azathioprine maintenance, resulting in complete resolution of skin lesions, normalization of urinalysis, and remission of immunologic activity over 4 months.
